pages.observation: The reading order is clear. The top row goes left then right, followed by the wide middle panel. In the bottom tier I read the tall left panel first, then the upper and lower right panels, which is the usual layout. Nothing pulled my eye out of order, and I did not see two nearby balloons that could be read in the wrong order. Only one speech balloon is on the page, and its tail correctly points to the labtech, not to Ravi. The teal labels have no tails, so I read them as screen or notification text. However, nothing drawn shows which device or screen each label belongs to. The "NEW PRESCRIPTION" label is low on the left, away from the pharmacist, and the reader cannot tell whose screen it is on. Ravi does not reply to "All done, Ravi!" A silent reaction is acceptable, but the placeholder cannot show whether he acknowledges it, so the final art should give him a visible reaction such as a nod. Continuity: the page opens with "Meanwhile," but without the previous page I cannot tell what this happens alongside, and the caption does not say who notified the pharmacy or lab, or why. The jump from "Later that day" (samples taken) to "Results ready" has no caption giving the time, so the time between the middle panel and the bottom tier is unclear. In panel 6, 'meera' appears without introduction. The caption speaks only of "The clinic", so a reader who has not met Meera before may not know who she is. Panels 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are all built the same way ("X is notified" plus a label), and "notified" appears five times, which reads repetitively. Fit: several lines run right up to the box border and may overflow once lettered. These are "notified." in the panel 2 caption, "collect" in the panel 2 label, "his" at the end of the middle caption's first line, "notified." in the panel 4 caption, and "notified" at the end of the panel 6 caption's first line. The tall bottom-left panel has a large empty area between the caption and the label for one small figure. All text was readable and no file was unreadable. Because the figures are placeholders, I could not judge faces, hands or gaze.
